source.title: CUDA Programming Guide 13.1.0 — Multi-Device Stream, Event, and Memory Copy Behavior

documented_behavior: cudaEventQuery and cudaEventSynchronize can operate on an event belonging to a device other than the calling thread's current device.
cudaStreamWaitEvent supports an event and stream belonging to different devices.
cudaEventRecord requires its stream and event to belong to the same device.
Kernel launches require the calling thread's current device to match the launch stream's device.

application_to_decode_head.completion_poll: The CUDA-only DecodeHeadWindow::done path can query its completion event without switching to the head device; launch, allocation, capture and resource cleanup retain device ownership scopes.
application_to_decode_head.producer_dependency: Each remote head stream waits on the source verifier's already-recorded producer event before reading the published Q8_1 handoff.
application_to_decode_head.backend_scope: This documentation establishes CUDA behavior only; the HIP device scope is retained.
application_to_decode_head.performance_status: Removing device switches reduces host API work per completion poll. The resulting decode speed change requires end-to-end measurement and is not established by the API documentation.
